evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-11-12"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-11-12". Without dueDate, the response had dueDate null. The value is a plain YYYY-MM-DD date with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/2 with {"dueDate":"2026-01-05"} returned 200 and dueDate "2026-01-05". PATCH with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 and dueDate null, so the date was removed.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30", "13.11.2026" and "2026-2-3" each returned 400. PATCH with dueDate "2026-02-30" also returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today (UTC) is 2026-11-13. I created todos due yesterday, today, tomorrow, with no date, and one past-due todo that I then marked done. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the todo due 2026-11-12. The todo due today, the future one, the one with no date and the done one were all excluded. In GET /todos the done todo showed overdue false.
evidence.AC5: In the browser at /, the list items showed 'past fällig 2026-11-12', 'today fällig 2026-11-13' and 'pastdone ✓ fällig 2026-01-01'. Items without a due date showed no date.
evidence.AC6: Only the item 'past fällig 2026-11-12 überfällig' carried the word überfällig. The today, future, no-date and done-past-due items did not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. After I clicked it, the list showed only the 'past' item, which was marked überfällig.
